# High RAM atlas — $D000-$FFFF, who writes what, when, on which machine

> Generated (D-RAMATLAS). Every row is a run of addresses with the same writers at the same moments on every machine below. **Moments:** b boot, I INIT (a cartridge's HIMEM claim), H H.RUNC (after the cartridge scan), D MSX-DOS running, B (Disk) BASIC running. **Writers:** M main ROM, D disk ROM, S zerobas's sub ROM, R code running from RAM (MSX-DOS, a BASIC program's machine code, RAM-resident routines). An empty cell: nothing wrote the range in that run. **zerobas** names the cells zerobas declares there (basic/, disk/; `(in X)`: inside a declared buffer).

> **Clean room:** the runs record the address written, the moment and the writing code's page@slot -- no value and no program counter, on any machine. So this page says WHO uses RAM, never WHAT a reference keeps in it; a class that needs values (what a published cell holds) comes from the published-cell probes.

> **Scenarios:** `dos`: test.dsk, 70 s, keys 16 s '⏎', 21 s 'DIR MSXDOS.SYS⏎', 26 s 'COPY MSXDOS.SYS X.SYS⏎', 32 s 'BASIC⏎', 44 s 'OPEN"Y.TXT"FOR OUTPUT AS', 52 s '10 A$=STRING$(50,65):B$='; `basic`: test720.dsk, 45 s, keys 10 s '⏎', 16 s 'OPEN"Y.TXT"FOR OUTPUT AS', 24 s '10 A$=STRING$(50,65):B$='; `plain`: no disk, 30 s, keys 10 s '10 A$=STRING$(50,65):B$='

> **Power-on:** the main ROM's writes before any cartridge's INIT are left out of the rows (they are the RAM test and clear, not a use of the RAM). Addresses of the range the main ROM writes at boot, per run: VG plain 12235, VGHBD dos 12235, VGHBD basic 12235, CF dos 12235, CF basic 12235, ZBND plain 3476, ZBD dos 3437, ZBD basic 3437.
